## The Spark: A Lifelong Fascination with Weather

Ever since I was little, my parents would constantly find me sitting in front of the TV, completely captivated by weather reports. While other kids were watching cartoons, I was drawn to the radar loops, the satellite views, and the meteorologists tracking cold fronts, squall lines, and tropical systems. 

That fascination naturally followed me into the classroom. Throughout science classes in late elementary and early middle school, I was always asking *why*—trying to understand what drove high and low pressure, what created thunderstorms, and how the atmosphere operated. Outside of class, I dove into independent research and study, reading whatever I could find about atmospheric science and meteorology. 

When the opportunity came to build this final project, choosing Tampa Bay's weather was a natural extension of a lifelong passion that started in my childhood living room.

---

## The Vision: Blending Exploration and Storytelling

A central goal of this project was to make sure it wasn't just raw data on one hand or pure narrative on the other. Instead, it bridges the two:

::: {.records-grid}
::: {.record-card}
<div class="record-title">Interactive Exploration</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.95rem; color: #475569; margin-top: 0.5rem; line-height: 1.5;">
Investigating over **100,000+ hourly observations** across a full decade (2015–2024) at Tampa International Airport (KTPA). Here, you can interact with multi-year temperature trends, dew point comfort zones, pressure distributions, and all-time station records.
</div>
:::

::: {.record-card}
<div class="record-title">Atmospheric Storytelling</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.95rem; color: #475569; margin-top: 0.5rem; line-height: 1.5;">
Weather is also a lived experience. In the story section, we zoom in to minute-by-minute and hourly telemetry during major tropical events—like **Hurricane Irma's eye passage in 2017**—unraveling the physical drama of barometric collapse and extreme gale winds.
</div>
:::
:::

By combining both perspectives:
- **Exploration** provides the empirical baseline: what is normal for Tampa Bay, what are the seasonal rhythms, and how rare are extreme events?
- **Story** brings the human and physical reality into focus: what does it actually feel like when a Category 4 or 5 cyclone churns up the Florida peninsula?

Together, they turn cold meteorological telemetry into a living, interactive analysis.

---

## Data & Methods

- **Primary Historical Dataset:** 10 years (2015–2024) of hourly surface meteorological records from the automated station at Tampa International Airport (KTPA), sourced via NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) Local Climatological Data (LCD).
- **Real-Time Data:** Live telemetry fetched dynamically from the National Weather Service (NWS) API.
- **Technology Stack:** Built using **R**, **Quarto**, and the **tidyverse** (`dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `plotly`, `leaflet`).
